title: Emergency Root Edits may skip the normal timeline, and disclosure can be withheld if it would endanger users
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.3.1 provides that in an Urgent or Emergency Situation as defined by the Sky Core Atlas (A.1.9.1.1), "the Operational Facilitator may allow a Root Edit to occur more quickly than the timeline specified above." Where feasible they "should announce the decision to deploy the emergency Root Edit protocol and provide their reasoning via a public Sky Forum post," "unless doing so would endanger Spark or its users."

The design deliberately separates the trigger from the definition: what counts as an emergency comes from the Core Atlas, not from Spark's own judgment, so the Agent cannot widen its own fast path by redefining urgency. What Spark controls is only how much of the normal timeline to compress once that external condition is met.

The disclosure carve-out is the sharpest trade-off in the provision. An exploit that is disclosed before it is patched is an exploit that gets used, so silence is sometimes the protective act. But the exception is self-assessed by the same actor exercising the emergency power, and its language is "should" rather than "must," leaving the accountability record weakest exactly where discretion is greatest.

Note also what is *not* relaxed: the provision speaks only to timeline and announcement. The alignment restriction of A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6 has no emergency exception.
description: The Facilitator may accelerate under Atlas-defined Urgent or Emergency Situations and should publish the reasoning — unless announcing it would itself endanger Spark or its users.
